operator_io_quirks: Mixed-case identifiers: tables 'event','journalist','news_report' lowercase but columns 'Event_ID','Date','Name','journalist_ID','Work_Type' mixed case; must double-quote with original spelling.
Column name collision: 'Name' exists in both event and journalist; 'journalist_ID' in journalist and news_report; 'Event_ID' in event and news_report — case-insensitive lookup must be table-scoped.
DDL uses backtick-quoted parent refs (`journalist`, `event`) in FK clauses; sqlite_master DDL replay must preserve them verbatim.
Tiny tables: event=5, journalist=11, news_report=7 rows — choose_table_sizes (min 30) will massively oversize vs original; no huge-table sampling needed.

Declared TEXT but integer-stored: journalist.Age is TEXT holding '37','27' etc (String fuzzer, but values are numeric strings); Date is TEXT holding '13 October 2008' (String fuzzer, not Date fuzzer).
Date column format 'D Month YYYY' (e.g. '13 October 2008') — not one of TS's 7 date templates; TS will treat as plain String and generate random charset strings, losing the date shape.
news_report composite PK (journalist_ID, Event_ID) — both members are also FK children; composite-PK member max_l0=30 applies to both.
news_report.journalist_ID distinct=6 but journalist has 11 rows; news_report.Event_ID distinct=5 = event rows — FK coverage partial, not full.
All columns notnull=0 (no NOT NULL constraints) — TS NULL injection won't be rejected by sqlite; no CHECK constraints.
No self-references, no dangling FKs, no non-unique parents — clean FK graph, 2-level topological order (event,journalist -> news_report).
journalist.Nationality distinct=3 (England/Wales/Northern Ireland) — low-cardinality enum-like; TS String fuzzer will not preserve this small set.
journalist.Years_working INT distinct=10 over 11 rows; Age TEXT distinct=8 — near-unique, TS Number/String perturbation may create implausible negatives.
operator_ts_expectations: Date column (TEXT, '13 October 2008'): dispatches to String fuzzer (type 'text' -> char family), NOT Date; TS emits random a-zA-Z0-9() strings of length ~[min,max] — destroys date semantics, likely FN on date-comparison queries.
Age (TEXT, numeric strings): String fuzzer; int-like strings get str(i±1) added to pool, so some plausible ages survive, but contaminate() adds random suffixes — FP risk on age-range predicates.
Nationality (TEXT, 3 values): String fuzzer with p=0.2 fresh draws — will invent nationalities not in {England,Wales,Northern Ireland}; FN on 'Nationality = X' queries where X is a real value.
Name columns (person names, event names): String fuzzer random charset — implausible names; FN on LIKE/equality on names, but ties preserved via element reuse.

Event_ID / journalist_ID (INT PKs): Number fuzzer, single-col PK -> max_l0=inf, so fresh draws unbounded; PK dedup keeps first occurrence; FK children draw from parent's final values with replacement — referential integrity preserved but many-to-one skew.
news_report composite PK: both members max_l0=30; sample_fresh_primary_keys drops duplicate (journalist_ID,Event_ID) tuples — may shrink news_report below chosen size.

Event_Attendance (INT, values 225..6650): Number fuzzer scale from 'int' -> scale=0, range [-1,1] full-range but list range [min(el), 10^0] quirk caps upper at 1 — TS will emit tiny/negative attendances, FN on 'attendance > N' queries.
Years_working (INT, 3..21): same Number scale=0 quirk — list_max overwritten to 1, so fresh draws in [-1,1]; implausible negatives, FN on range predicates.
Small tables (5-11 rows) vs TS min size 30: TS instances much larger than original; COUNT(*) queries will differ in magnitude but denotation (non-empty, ordering) often preserved.
No NOT NULL: TS NULL injection (p=0.2, or p=0 whole instance w.p. 0.3) inserts NULLs freely; queries with IS NULL / IS NOT NULL may flip.

FK consistency: news_report rows always reference existing event/journalist IDs (drawn from parent final values) — join queries preserve referential semantics; but parent PK dedup may leave some child IDs orphaned if parent shrank after draw (upstream draws from final, so safe).
String contaminate() (p=0.5) on Venue/Name/Work_Type adds/removes chars — breaks exact-match and LIKE-prefix queries; Work_Type (3 values) especially vulnerable.
